title: Quant Pilot Lab Notebook — Retail POC
content:
Context:
- Customer: mid-market retail analytics SaaS considering private (on-prem) inference for customer support chat and SKU summarization.
- Objective: Find a model + quantization + prompt pipeline that meets p99 <= 150ms for 128-token responses on a single 48GiB GPU node, maintain pragmatic quality (human proxy >= 3.8/5), and keep token unit costs low for committed infra.
- Constraints: air-gapped deployment, KMS-managed keys, 1024 token recommended user context cap to preserve headroom.

Experiment design:
- Candidate families limited to 7B-14B open families that compress to fit 48GiB after quantization.
- Quant methods: NF4, AWQ (GptQ-style), Q4_K_M, and INT8 dynamic. Measure both footprint and runtime jitter.
- Pipelines tested: 1) direct chat, 2) RAG (dense retrieval -> generator), 3) rerank+generate (bi-encoder -> cross-encoder rerank -> generator).
- Evaluation: 200 customer-sampled queries for automated semantic-similarity metrics + 6 human evaluators for borderline outputs. Warmup of 32 requests before perf capture.

Model candidates (internal labels):
- oak-13b (base 13B open)
- maple-13b-instruct (instruction-tuned variant)
- spruce-7b-fast (compact 7B)
- birch-14b-sparse (sparse-optimized 14B)
- elm-8b-embed (fast embedder for retrieval)

Conversion & profiling snippets (lab commands used):
- Quant convert example:
  python tools/quantize.py --input /mnt/models/oak-13b --out /tmp/oak-awq --scheme awq --bits 4 --group 128
- Server run (single request profiling):
  ./rwinference --model /tmp/oak-awq --max_tokens 128 --batch_size 1 --context 1024 --kv-mode dynamic --stream=false
- Perf capture: rwinf-prof --samples 250 --trace p99,p95,p50 --out perf_oak_awq.csv

Summary of key runs (representative):
- spruce-7b-fast + nf4: p50 35ms, p95 60ms, p99 105ms, GPU 11.3GiB, human 3.7/5. Best latency/cost but weaker on long-form accuracy.
- oak-13b + awq: p50 58ms, p95 110ms, p99 155ms, GPU 22.1GiB, human 4.2/5. Close to latency goal; kernel tuning expected to reduce p99 by 10-25ms.
- maple-13b-instruct + int8: p50 52ms, p95 95ms, p99 138ms, GPU 20.0GiB, human 4.0/5. Observed CPU dequantization spikes causing jitter (~10% of requests).
- birch-14b-sparse + q4_k_m: p50 88ms, p95 175ms, p99 240ms, GPU 30.8GiB, human 4.4/5. High quality but not viable on single node without fragmentation.
- Rerank pipeline (elm-8b embed + oak-13b gen): end-to-end p50 68ms, p95 115ms, p99 142ms, effective GPU ~26GiB if retrieval cached, human 4.3/5. Caching embeddings reduces user-path work significantly.

Observations / tradeoffs:
- 7B + NF4 provides the most headroom for low-latency endpoints but shows higher hallucination rates on obscure inventory queries. Good for short response endpoints.
- AWQ on 13B gives the best quality/latency balance once kernels are tuned. Group-size and per-channel layout materially affect p99.
- INT8 yields good latency and quality but introduces occasional CPU-bound stalls; mitigate with dequant worker threads and prioritized IO.
- KV-cache memory dominates at >1024 context; recommend limiting live user context to 1024 for latency-constrained endpoints and using prefix caching for conversation history.
- Micro-batching windows (10-15ms) can add throughput without perceptible latency increase; tune per-route.

Prompt and pipeline lessons:
- Keep system prompt minimal: one short instruction + 1 exemplar. Longer system prompts increase both token cost and KV pressure.
- Retrieval: chunk size ~400-600 tokens with 30-80 token overlap depending on document density. Hybrid sparse+dense retrieval reduces noisy returns.
- Rerank: bi-encoder (elm-8b-embed) as filter, cross-encoder only on top-5 to reduce generator invocations.
- Safety: run light post-generation filters; pre-generation blocks often suppress legitimate phrasing in retail domain.

Action items / next tests:
- Re-run oak-13b AWQ with group-size 64 and alternate kernel build (PR 412) to measure p99 delta.
- Benchmark async micro-batching with 8-12ms windows to quantify throughput/latency sweet spot.
- Add daily eval harness in customer's environment to capture drift; trigger alert if semantic-proxy drops by >=0.25.
- Run full private-deployment QA on customer's AMI/driver stack (must include exact CUDA/cuDNN).

Deployment suggestion (pilot):
- Pilot config: maple-13b-instruct quantized to INT8, RAG pipeline using elm-8b embeddings, context cap 1024, async micro-batching (10ms), rerank top-5.
- If pilot p99 > 160ms or quality < 3.9/5, switch to oak-13b AWQ + kernel optimizations and enable KV-prefix caching.
- Observability: per-route p50/p95/p99, human-proxy score, cache hit ratio, and dequant CPU spikes flagged.

Risks / open questions:
- Production traffic shape may differ; recommend 7-day live sampling before full scale.
- Customer AMI kernel availability could limit optimized builds; plan for fallback kernels and verify with infra before rollout.
- Human-eval cadence and proxies need to be defined for automated alerts.

Notes for workshop demo:
- Bring live rerank pipeline demo with cached embeddings and a short slide showing perf vs quality tradeoffs.
- Prepare warmup script (32 requests) and the 200-query seed set for customer QA.
